tasks.short: Gather anonymous figures and examples from the caseload, attend committees, write position notes and organise with residents' groups.

steps.what: Social worker collects figures and examples of client problems from colleagues and files
Social worker serves on policy-making committees and community development meetings
Social worker writes position notes and letters lobbying for solutions

loop.input: The worker's key points, the anonymised caseload figures and the committee's question.
loop.output: A one-page position note with the problem, figures and proposed solutions.
loop.check: Code checks that every figure in the draft matches the anonymised export and that no name, address, date of birth or case number appears; the worker rewrites the argument and signs it.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the worker writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each note argues a different case; templates give only headings.

steps.what: Social worker meets client groups and residents to organise action

tasks.design: Anonymised counts per problem domain (debt, housing, school absence) come from the structured assessments in the youth care case system ({OTHER}) instead of asking colleagues. A bounded step drafts a position note from the worker's points and those counts, with code checking figures and stripping personal details; committees and community work stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures for policy work were gathered by asking around and reading files.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured case records can be counted, and language models draft short notes from bullet points.
tasks.still_hard: Small numbers can identify families in a small area; arguments must be the worker's own.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a council committee what poverty does to a child in a way they remember.

ambition.what: Caseload trends brought to the municipality every quarter, not only when asked.

reach.learn: Whether quarterly caseload trends change policy priorities.

evidence.claim: Youth care staff spend about 38% of their time on administration, the most of client-facing jobs.
Data about clients' health and problems is special-category data; figures must be anonymised before they leave the team.
Language models draft short notes from bullet points that a person then rewrites.

assumptions: Boundary: from preparing input to community action; council decisions are outside.
Input contract: anonymised counts exported from structured assessments by the information manager; counts under ten are suppressed; fallback is asking colleagues.
No client data goes into the drafting step.
unknowns: How often the worker sits on committees.
research_questions: Do figure-based notes change committee decisions?

incremental.description: Social worker checks the anonymised counts make sense.
Information manager runs the quarterly anonymised export.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meetings and organising in person.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect income and household documents, check them against scheme rules, weigh special circumstances, decide, explain and send the decision letter.

steps.what: Client gathers income, rent and household documents for the application
Social worker collects income, rent and household documents from the client
Social worker checks documents against scheme rules and calculates financial assistance by hand
Social worker weighs special circumstances to determine clients' eligibility
Social worker explains the outcome to the client
Social worker writes the decision letter

tasks.design: Clients upload documents against a checklist in the municipality's client portal ({GOV_PORTAL}), and a rules calculator built from the published scheme criteria and norms shows the indicated entitlement with each rule it applied. The worker weighs special circumstances and decides; the letter fills from the decision and the rules applied, and no AI is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents came on paper and the entitlement was worked out by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Rules calculators on published criteria are plain code; client portals take document uploads.
tasks.still_hard: Rules must be tested and kept current; special circumstances are judgement; a wrong formula hurts many families.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a family's real situation is not what the documents show.
tasks.altitude: The worker checks a calculation instead of doing it; the decision stays with the worker.

reach.learn: Whether shared rules give the same outcome across teams.

evidence.claim: AI that evaluates eligibility for public assistance is high-risk; this design uses rules only, no AI.
No decision with significant effect may be based solely on automated processing; the worker decides.
An inspectorate found probation risk formulas had been swapped since 2018, putting about 21% of cases in another risk category; use was paused in February 2026.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the decision letter; payment is outside.
Input contract: scheme criteria and norms coded and tested by the municipality's rules owner; documents uploaded by clients; fallback is paper and hand calculation.
Rules owner time is outside the worker's savings.
Weighing circumstances and explaining do not change.
Clients' upload time is priced as customer time, not as the worker's savings.
unknowns: Share of clients who can upload documents.
research_questions: Do outcomes vary less between workers with shared rules?

already_counted.description: Social worker checks the applied rules for each case.

incremental.description: Social worker helps clients upload documents.
Rules owner tests and updates the rules when schemes change.
Clients scan and upload their documents against the checklist in the portal (work moved from the social worker's collecting).

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Clients with complex income or no digital access keep the work manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The family social worker keeps advocacy and eligibility judgement; collecting figures and calculating shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using anonymised figures in policy work
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who brings real caseload trends to policy and gives families an answer on assistance in one visit.

job.title: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
